verdict: MGM's resorts took in $4.2B, but soft Las Vegas room rates left the quarter near break-even — a $17M loss for MGM's own shareholders, because $56M of the profit belonged to partners in jointly owned resorts.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs -$1.05 a year ago (that quarter had a $256M goodwill write-off)

kpis.label: MGM China market share
kpis.note: record quarterly revenue and share in Macau

segments.name: Casino
segments.note: Slots and table games across Las Vegas, regional U.S. resorts and Macau — roughly flat year over year.

segments.name: Rooms
segments.note: Hotel rooms — revenue fell as Las Vegas room rates softened in the quarter.

segments.name: Food and beverage
segments.note: Restaurants, bars and catering across the resorts.

segments.name: Entertainment, retail & other
segments.note: Shows, nightclubs, shops and other resort income.

opex.note: Running the resorts day to day — staff and operations not tied to one department.

opex.note: Wearing-out cost of the resorts, systems and intangibles.

opex.name: Property transactions & preopening, net
opex.note: Small net cost from property items and preopening, net.

otherDetail: Income from unconsolidated affiliates of $31M and $8M of other income, less $103M of net interest expense and $2M of non-operating losses from affiliates.
follow100Note: MGM kept nothing this quarter: after a small tax benefit, $1.33 of every $100 of profit went to joint-venture partners, leaving a $0.40 loss per $100 for MGM's own shareholders.
oneTimers: The year-ago quarter included a $256M goodwill impairment, which is why EPS improved from -$1.05 to -$0.07 despite a softer business. This quarter had no comparable charge.

takeaways.title: Las Vegas rates were the drag
takeaways.text: Rooms revenue fell 4% as Strip room rates softened (management said October rebounded). Casino revenue was flat at $2.3B despite the softer visitation economics.

takeaways.title: Macau set records
takeaways.text: MGM China posted record quarterly revenue and a record 17.1% market share in Macau, and regional U.S. resorts grew 1% on a same-store basis — the offsets to Las Vegas softness.

takeaways.title: Partners took the profit
takeaways.text: Consolidated net income was $39M, but $56M of profit belonged to noncontrolling partners (notably in MGM China), leaving a $17M loss attributable to MGM shareholders.

footerNote: MGM counts $31M of income from unconsolidated affiliates inside its reported operating income of $119M; here that $31M sits in other income, so the chart's operating profit line is $88M. Figures are rounded to $M from the release's thousands presentation; $1M of rounding is absorbed in casino revenue. The tax line is a $17M benefit (money back), which is why it adds to profit.
